files.content:
import { OverlayArrow as AriaOverlayArrow } from 'react-aria-components'
import type { OverlayArrowProps as AriaOverlayArrowProps } from 'react-aria-components'

/**
 * The shape of the marker: a rotated square with two hairlines and the panel's own fill, so it continues
 * the panel's edge out to a point. Every other surface here is squared; an SVG arrow would be the one
 * curved thing in the system.
 *
 * **The rotation is on the shape inside React Aria's element, not on the element itself.** That element is
 * positioned with an inline `transform`, and an inline style outranks every class — a `rotate-45` written
 * on it type-checks, looks right in the source, and does nothing at all. The first version of this file did
 * exactly that and rendered an unrotated square sitting on the panel's edge.
 *
 * The two edges facing outward are the ones kept, so the other two disappear under the panel. Which two
 * depends on where React Aria put the overlay, which it reports as `data-placement` on the **parent** —
 * hence the arbitrary ancestor variants rather than plain `data-[…]` ones.
 */
export const OVERLAY_ARROW = [
  'block size-2 rotate-45 border-line-strong bg-panel',
  '[[data-placement=bottom]_&]:border-t [[data-placement=bottom]_&]:border-l',
  '[[data-placement=top]_&]:border-r [[data-placement=top]_&]:border-b',
  '[[data-placement=left]_&]:border-t [[data-placement=left]_&]:border-r',
  '[[data-placement=right]_&]:border-b [[data-placement=right]_&]:border-l',
].join(' ')

/** React Aria positions this element; all it needs from us is to stay above the panel. */
export const OVERLAY_ARROW_POSITION = 'z-10'

/**
 * The marker that points from a floating panel back at the thing that opened it.
 *
 * ```tsx
 * <Popover>
 *   <Popover.Arrow />
 *   …
 * </Popover>
 * ```
 *
 * **Nothing here uses one by default, and that is a decision rather than an oversight.** A pointer is a
 * shape the design language does not otherwise contain: the sheet's panels are flat rectangles joined to
 * their trigger by proximity and position, and every menu, select and tooltip in this system opens
 * anchored without one. So it is an opt-in slot — `Popover.Arrow`, `Tooltip.Arrow` — for the case where a
 * panel must be tied to a small target and proximity is not enough.
 *
 * React Aria positions this element and reports which way it must point as `data-placement`.
 */
export interface OverlayArrowProps extends Omit<
  AriaOverlayArrowProps,
  'className'
> {
  className?: string
}

export function OverlayArrow({ className, ...props }: OverlayArrowProps) {
  return (
    <AriaOverlayArrow
      data-slot="overlay-arrow"
      className={OVERLAY_ARROW_POSITION}
      {...props}
    >
      <span
        data-slot="overlay-arrow-shape"
        className={[OVERLAY_ARROW, className].filter(Boolean).join(' ')}
      />
    </AriaOverlayArrow>
  )
}

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-select-menu`, shared by everything that opens over the page: `Menu` now, and
 * `Select` and `ComboBox` when they converge onto it. The same split as `field.ts` — the surface is
 * the thing that must not drift, and the slots are still defined per component so Storybook
 * documents them under the right name.
 *
 * The shadow is the one literal colour in this file: it is a **shadow**, not a surface, and every
 * attempt to derive one from a token produces a haze rather than a shadow. It is `rgba(0,0,0,.7)`
 * because a shadow has to darken in both themes, exactly as the modal's scrim does.
 */
export const SURFACE = [
  'border border-line-strong bg-panel',
  'shadow-[0_12px_32px_rgba(0,0,0,.7)]',
  'outline-none',
].join(' ')

/** A popover that holds a single scrolling list, sized to the control it came from. */
export const POPOVER = `flex w-(--trigger-width) flex-col overflow-hidden ${SURFACE}`

/** The list inside it. `max-h` so a long list scrolls rather than running off the page. */
export const LIST = 'max-h-[264px] overflow-auto p-0 outline-none'

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-select-option`: 13px at 75%, with the accent reserved for the choice.
 *
 * Hover and focus land on the same treatment on purpose. A menu is walked with the arrow keys as
 * much as with a pointer, so the row the keyboard has reached and the row the pointer is over
 * should not look like two different kinds of thing.
 */
export const ITEM = [
  'relative flex items-center justify-between gap-3',
  'px-3.5 py-[11px] text-[13px] text-fg/75',
  'cursor-pointer select-none',
  'data-[hovered]:bg-fg/7 data-[hovered]:text-fg',
  'data-[focus-visible]:outline-none data-[focus-visible]:bg-fg/7 data-[focus-visible]:text-fg',
  'data-[selected]:text-teal',
  'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:text-fg/35',
].join(' ')

/** One item's text, which truncates rather than wrapping a menu wider than its trigger. */
export const ITEM_LABEL = 'truncate'

/** A run of items, announced as a group. */
export const SECTION = 'flex flex-col'

/** The sheet's `.ds-select-group-label`. */
export const SECTION_TITLE = [
  'px-3.5 pt-[9px] pb-1',
  'text-[11px] uppercase tracking-[0.08em] text-fg/45',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet's `.ds-div-hair`, inset so it reads as a break in the list rather than a table edge. */
export const SEPARATOR = 'my-1 h-px shrink-0 bg-line'

/** A search box above the list sits behind the menu's own hairline, so it reads as part of the surface. */
export const SEARCH = 'border-b border-line-strong p-2'

/**
 * A submenu's caret. A row with a submenu says so — `data-has-submenu` is React Aria's — and an
 * affordance nobody can see is not an affordance.
 */
export const SUBMENU_CARET = [
  'shrink-0 text-fg/45',
  'transition-[rotate] duration-[120ms] ease-pulse',
  'data-[open]:rotate-90',
].join(' ')

docs:
A panel anchored to the thing that opened it, that does not take the page away.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <Button>Filters</Button>
  <Popover.Content placement="bottom start">
    <Popover.Title>Filters</Popover.Title>
    <Popover.Description>Applies to this view only.</Popover.Description>
  </Popover.Content>
</Popover>
```

| Slot                  | React Aria           | Notes                                           |
| --------------------- | -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `Popover`             | `DialogTrigger`      | The trigger, then a `Popover.Content`           |
| `Popover.Content`     | `Popover` + `Dialog` | The surface, and the dialog that names it       |
| `Popover.Title`       | `Heading`            | The modal's own title type, imported not copied |
| `Popover.Description` | `Text`               | `aria-describedby` wired here, as on Modal      |

**A popover is a modal that is not modal**, and that is the whole decision. It is dismissed by Escape
and by a click outside, but it traps nothing and hides nothing: the page behind stays readable and
usable. Reach for `Modal` when the page is irrelevant to the decision and for this when it is the
context.

The surface is `popover.ts`'s, but **not `POPOVER` itself** — that one is `w-(--trigger-width)`, which
is right for a select matched to its field and wrong for a panel with its own idea of how wide it
should be. It is what `Menu`, `Select` and `ComboBox` are built on; this is the same surface with no
list at all.

**Placement is a request, not an instruction.** `placement="bottom start"` opens downwards when there
is room and flips when there is not, so the story asserts that React Aria reports where the panel
landed rather than the value the prop asked for.

### The browser probe reports "open on load", and is wrong

Worth writing down because it has now happened twice and cost a component once.

A throwaway Playwright script that navigates straight to an `iframe.html?viewMode=story` URL and then
looks for `role="dialog"` **finds one already open**, for both the sheet and the popover — because
Storybook has restored that story's canvas from a previous visit in the same browser context. The
test runner does not: `Default` clicks the trigger and its **first** assertion, made before any click,
is that no dialog is present — and it passes.

**So the runner is the authority on whether something opens by itself, and the probe is not.** The
`Sheet` was removed on this evidence in an earlier round; its size defect was independently confirmed
and stands, but the "opens before you open it" half of that verdict may well have been this artifact.
Trust the suite for state, the screenshot for appearance.
